IBEW.text:
**Trampin the IBEW Indoor Locals — Monday, August 3, 2026**

**LU-291 Boise, ID** is running hot with **$65.33/hr** at VECA Electric on the META KND 3&5 project, plus an incentive program with OT premium pay locked in. Prime Controls, Quality Electric, and Lea Electric are all feeding the Micron ID1 site at **$45.33/hr** with **$170/day per diem** (7 days if eligible)—PLA work, and Lea's hiring start is *today or tomorrow*. Book depth is thick at 132 hands across just 17 calls; this one's moving fast.

**LU-481 Indianapolis, IN** has the Google Data Center Mooresville job running wide open—Ermco's got **55 Inside JW slots** at top scale **$54.75/hr**, 5-10s plus Saturday 8s with *all OT double time*. Malarchy Shingles Factory adds another **10 JW** same contractor, same hours. Book's 170 hands deep on 36 calls; steady stream.

**LU-1426 Grand Forks, ND** is printing money on the Polaris Forge Data Center in Harwood. Parsons Electric running **78 JW** at **$44.80/hr** base plus **$100/day non-taxed per diem** (Monday–Friday), stepping to **$150 Sat/Sun**. That's 6-10s with incentive stacking hard. Hunt Electric's also hiring **10 JW** at the Air Base with the same rate plus ND license bonus. 117 hands on 21 calls—board's moving.

**LU-613 Atlanta, GA** is fat: **53 calls**, ~331 hands. Inglett & Stubbs dominates with **44 JW** at the QTS Fayette data center (**$40/hr**, 4-10s & 2-8s), plus **22 JW** at Wellstar Paulding Hospital. Miller Electrical's medium-voltage splicer work pays **$40.90/hr**. Top scale is **$48/hr**, but the volume is what kills here.

**LU-401 Reno, NV**: Bechtel's Thacker Pass in Winnemucca is *open*—**47 Inside JW** slots at top scale **$57.39/hr** plus **$30/day per diem**. Baker Electric's modular solar install work in Yerington adds **14 JW**. Book's 129 hands on 14 calls.

**LU-1105 Newark, OH** is humming data center and fab work—Superior Group's got **40 JW** spread across three CMH sites at **$683/hr** scale (yes, you read that), starting 6am with 4-10s most Saturdays. Bechtel's Project Cardinal in New Albany adds **10 more** with a **$300/day** notation.

The board's chasing data centers and fab work—Wisconsin, Idaho, North Dakota, Ohio. That's where the hands are going and the OT's printing.

LINEMAN.text:
**Trampin the IBEW Lineman Locals — Monday, August 3, 2026**

**LU-71 Columbus, OH** is running hot with 46 calls and roughly 140 hands on the board. NEW RIVER ELECT. CORP. is pushing 40 JW linemen into Columbus distro work at **top scale** with $125 nightly PD and $125 bonuses on 10-hour days—6-10s, CDL required. Another 9 slots open in Southern Ohio on 4-10s with optional weekend extensions. CAPITAL ELECTRIC LINE BUILDERS needs 6 more with cable-splicing chops in Johnstown. This local is moving.

**LU-1426 Grand Forks, ND** has 21 calls for 117 hands, anchored by the Polaris Forge Data Center push in Harwood. Parsons Electric alone is hiring 78 JW inside wiremen at **$44.80/hr** with **$100/day non-taxed per diem**, 6-10s, and weekend incentive pay ($100 Mon-Fri, $150 Sat-Sun). GPS radius is 100+ miles. Hunt Electric and Northern Valley adding another 14 slots at the same scale on Air Base work.

**LU-175 Chattanooga, TN** shows 14 calls against 107 hands—tightest book here. Adman Electric is spinning up the DNN4 Data Center with 50 total JW slots split day/night shift, 12-hour rotations, rotating weekends. Lawson Electric in Dalton, Georgia adds 13 more. Day and Zimmermann posted 10 for Watts Bar Nuclear (TVA MODS work, requires nuclear cert).

**LU-583 El Paso, TX** has 10 calls chasing 98 hands. Summit Line, Cupertino Electric, and B & D Industries all posting JW slots at **$55/hr** with NM State JIW License EE98J required, OSHA 10, and **all OT double time**. Rosendin at **$40 + $15 incentive** for 90% of a 60-hour week.

**LU-291 Boise, ID** is flooded: 19 calls, 136 hands. Three separate contractors (Prime Controls, Quality Electric, Lea Electric) hiring 88 combined JW inside wiremen for the Micron ID1 Idaho PLA job at **$45.33/hr + $20/hr adder**, **$170/day per diem x 7 days** if eligible. VECA Electric's META Idaho gig tops out at **$65.33/hr** with incentive OT.

Data-center and PLA work is vacuuming hands across the Mountain West and upper South; transmission and distro rebuild is holding Ohio and the Midwest.

UA.text:
**Trampin the UA Locals — Monday, August 3, 2026**

**LU-140 Salt Lake City, UT** is moving 18 calls with 61 hands in the funnel — serious velocity. BCS Mechanical's Sego Project in West Valley is eating 28 slots (15 pipefitters, 13 plumbers, 5 apprentices) on straight 4-10s starting today, and DSI's QTS data center in Eagle Mountain has 6 more journeyman fitters working variable 5-10s with a single 8-hour day mixed in. No scale posted, but the volume here is the story: this board's churning.

**LU-776 Lima, OH** has 10 calls stacked with 46 hands available — industrial shutdown and fab work. Bmwc's Nutrien shutdown is recruiting 12 hands (pipefitters, dayshift, 7-12s) with **$11/hr incentive on straight time and $16.50/hr on OT/double time if under 50 miles, or $150/day per diem if over 50 miles**. Graham's Cenovus maintenance and Gem's fab shop round out the board with welders and combo fitters. DI and DISA cards are mandatory across most calls.

**LU-290 Portland, OR** is the specialty play: 21 calls, 30 hands, but they're hunting orbital welders, BIM detailers, and commercial refrigeration techs. Charter Mechanical's Intel Ronler Acres tool install is chasing 4 orbital welders; Apollo and Harder Mechanical need BIM detailers at foreman scale. Tight skill gaps here mean less competition for qualified hands.

**LU-208 Denver, CO** posts 15 calls for 37 bodies. Apollo's DC2 data center in Aurora needs 10 fitters on 6-10 day shifts; US Engineering's Fort Collins Broadcom job wants 4 high-purity fitters with tube bending chops. Solid commercial rate work without the refinery grind.

**LU-525 Las Vegas, NV** sits light at 1 call but it's clean: Four Seasons towers in Henderson, 12 journeyman slots, OSHA 10/30 card required. Thin board but zero competition.

Data centers and industrial shutdowns are pulling hands inland — West, Midwest, and Mountain time zones dominate the calls.
